rule: The blind pass scores transcription-channel fit, morphology, chronology, geography, free parameters and independent criticism without using the traditional Chinese word-by-word glosses. Semantics are added only in the reveal pass.

models.name: Old Arin / Yeniseian
models.analysis_source: VOVIN2016; refined toward Arin by BONMANN_FRIES

evidence.claim: A published whole-phrase Yeniseian reconstruction can be mapped onto all four Chinese chunks without changing language family mid-phrase.
The two predicate-sized chunks independently end in an -aŋ-like sequence compatible with Yeniseian finite morphology.
The second predicate's -taŋ sequence has a specifically Arin parallel as a third-person plural ending.
Connecting the stable Chinese ke syllable to Arin kel requires loss/non-representation of a liquid coda in Chinese transcription.
The earlier Pumpokol-style Yeniseian solution was criticized for unattested morphemes and unmatched units; the newer Arin refinement must clear this legacy objection rather than inherit a free pass.
An Old Arin stage is chronologically compatible with the early fourth-century setting proposed for the Jie material.
Independent contact research supports Yeniseian-Turkic interaction in Inner Asia and later Old Arin/Common Turkic contact as historically plausible.
After gloss reveal, Arin kel is unusually close in both vowel shape and meaning to the syllable ke glossed as army.
After gloss reveal, the proposed Yeniseian predicate analyses reproduce the transmitted event-level interpretation.
A published Turkic reconstruction covers the entire phrase and supplies an internally Turkic morphosyntactic parse.
Final -ŋ has a plausible Turkic imperative comparison and is not by itself diagnostic for Yeniseian.
The authors explicitly note that reconstructed erkan does not conform to the Old Turkic vowel-harmony system they posit.
The boklug-gu accusative analysis requires reconstructive assumptions about a pre-Old-Turkic accusative history not directly attested in the phrase.
The published parse maps 支 to a zero nominative in su-Ø, leaving one written syllabic character without an audible lexical segment.
Later historical-linguistic critiques argue that the modern Turkic readings are difficult to reconcile with the Chinese transcription and current Turkic historical phonology.
An archaic Turkic variety is not excluded on chronology alone.
Turkic-Yeniseian contact and Turkic-speaking groups in the broader Inner Asian zone are independently plausible.
After gloss reveal, Turkic sü provides a direct army comparison.
After gloss reveal, Turkic ket- provides a direct leave/depart comparison.
After gloss reveal, the full proposed Turkic sentence tracks the transmitted event-level meaning.

models.name: Yeniseian-Turkic contact model
models.analysis_source: No published mixed-language parse of this exact phrase is treated as established here.

evidence.claim: Bidirectional early Turkic-Yeniseian lexical contact is independently supported by controlled loanword analysis.
Old Arin/Common Turkic contact in roughly the third-fourth century CE is historically defensible.
Contact does not itself demonstrate that this ten-character sentence switches language families internally.
Within-phrase family switching is penalized unless an independent boundary or borrowing diagnostic is supplied.
The broader contact geography is plausible.
The broader contact chronology is plausible.
Later witnesses show real corruption at the 劬/助/句又 locus and digital OCR can corrupt 羯/褐/羌-like labels.
The main witness family preserves a highly stable ten-character core and the label 此羯語也, so total unrecoverability is too strong as a default.
Repeated final nasal structure in predicate-sized chunks is non-random evidence that the string may retain recoverable morphology.
The analysis freely switches among unrelated language families to maximize local resemblance.
Several comparisons rely on much later forms without a demonstrated fourth-century chain.
No single-language whole-phrase morphology is recovered.

ablations.description: Blind evidence with later scholarly verdict/critique removed
Second pass after revealing transmitted Chinese glosses

guardrails: A model may lead only because one dimension is carrying it; ablation stability must be reported.
Contact plausibility cannot be used as permission for arbitrary phrase-level code-switching.
Semantic matches are forbidden in BLIND_ALL and are added only in GLOSS_REVEAL.
